description: Pins protocol::encode_share_import_blob_raw + protocol::decode_share_import_blob byte mapping for the MYF1 share-import staging blob codec (§9.20). The blob seals an arbitrary-binary framed-file record (filename + declared MIME + file bytes, framed by the core layer) under a device-local wrap_key — the codec is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC and vault-agnostic: it never runs Argon2id and binds NEITHER account_number_hash NOR items_key_id (the queue is created while the vault is locked, or from a separate OS share-extension sandbox that does not hold root_key). It binds the per-entry share_id (also the queue filename) via aad_share_import_blob (AAD role 'share-import-blob'); there is NO HKDF SubkeyRole (a root_key-derived KEK would be wrong — the queue must survive while root_key is unavailable). ciphertext_len is variable (plaintext_len + 32), capped at MAX_SHARE_IMPORT_PLAINTEXT_LEN (64 MiB, matching the MYA1 attachment cap); an oversize ciphertext_len is a CiphertextLenOverflow reject before allocation. The MYF1 magic is a free-pool §10.3 allocation (F=file, MYND-507), implementer-chosen like every family magic. 11 cases: 2 encrypt (short binary + non-UTF-8 binary) + 1 decrypt_ok + 3 decrypt_aead_fail (tag-tamper + cross-share_id + wrong-wrap-key, all non-distinguishing per §6.4) + 5 parse_fail (one per distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject). Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_share_import_blob_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/share_import_blob.rs).

cases.description: Encode a short binary shared file (10 bytes, PNG-ish magic incl. an embedded NUL + 0xFF) under the device-local wrap_key. Expected blob = 49-byte header + plaintext_len + 32-byte CTX tag.

Encode a genuinely non-UTF-8 binary payload (lone 0x80 continuation, 0xC0, a surrogate encoding 0xED 0xA0 0x80, an out-of-range 0xF4 0x90 0x80 0x80) to pin byte transparency — this codec seals OPAQUE bytes (unlike MYK1's dictated UTF-8) — and a different variable ciphertext_len.

Round-trip the short-binary blob back to the framed-file plaintext under the matching wrap_key. Proves the decoder's header parse + AEAD unwrap (share_id read from the header, bound into the AAD) reconstruct the exact bytes.
Take the short-binary blob and flip the final byte (inside the 32-byte CTX commitment tag) via XOR 0xFF. The decoder MUST surface a non-distinguishing CannotDecrypt (spec §6.4).
cases.informational_tamper_description: final byte (inside CTX tag) flipped via XOR 0xFF

cases.description: Take the short-binary blob and flip one byte of the header share_id (offset 5). Any 16-byte id is structurally valid, so this passes the header checks — but share_id is read from the header and bound into the AAD (§9.20.3), so the AEAD verification fails. Proves an entry cannot be relabelled / swapped to another share_id slot.
cases.informational_tamper_description: header share_id byte at offset 5 flipped via XOR 0x01; AAD-bound

cases.description: Take the intact short-binary blob but decrypt under a DIFFERENT device wrap_key (0x01×32 instead of 0x42×32). Collapses to the same CannotDecrypt; ports MUST NOT distinguish.
cases.informational_tamper_description: intact blob decrypted under wrong wrap_key (0x01×32)

cases.description: First byte of the MYF1 magic corrupted to 'X'. Rejected at offset 0 before any decryption (magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline, §9.20.3).
protocol_version byte (offset 4) set to 0x02 instead of 0x01. A v0.1 decoder rejects an unknown protocol version before decrypting.

ciphertext_len field (offset 45..49) set to 0xFFFFFFFF (4 GiB), far over the MAX_SHARE_IMPORT_PLAINTEXT_LEN + 32 cap (64 MiB + 32). Rejected BEFORE allocation so a hostile length cannot trigger a huge allocation (contrast the fixed-size vault-quickunlock, which rejects any length != 64).
Only the 4-byte MYF1 magic, no room for the 49-byte header. Rejected before any field read.
Valid header advertising ciphertext_len = plaintext + 32, but the blob is one byte shorter than header + ciphertext_len. Rejected before the AEAD stage.
